choices.content: When two lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal
When two lines are parallel, interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two nonadjacent interior angles

question.prompt: When proving that the interior angles of a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\), a line parallel to \(BC\) is drawn through vertex \(A\). Which fact is mainly used?

solutions.explanation: Draw \(DE\parallel BC\) through \(A\). Then \(\angle B=\angle BAD\) and \(\angle C=\angle CAE\) (alternate interior angles are equal). Together with \(\angle BAC\), they form a straight angle of \(180^\circ\).
solutions.title: Transfer angles using a parallel line
